audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings do not reflect the June 2026 debt burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $323.0 million debt increase; approximately $17.1 million annual pretax interest at the filed 5.3% rate
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation combines a 2025 OE numerator with June 2026 debt and shares, while equity-level OE must include interest on all debt in the same perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had total borrowings outstanding under our Amended Credit Agreement of $ 511.0 million, consisting of $ 121.0 million outstanding under the Revolver and $ 390.0 million outstanding under the Term Loan.
audit_findings.explanation: A temporal-perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: debt rose from $511 million to $834 million after the OE period. The missing interest could materially reduce OE, but the net direction is mixed because the borrowings also funded acquisitions and repurchases whose earnings and share effects must be included consistently.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $323 million increase by use of proceeds, construct a June 2026 pro forma earnings perimeter including acquired earnings and full run-rate after-tax interest, and rerun all scenarios with perimeter-consistent shares.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized software spending may be omitted from maintenance reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.647 million capitalized software spending in FY2025; $10.065 million in H1 2026; filed 2026 combined property, equipment and software forecast of $35 million to $40 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back software amortization without deducting the maintenance portion of capitalized development and cloud-implementation cash spending overstates OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate that cash utilized for purchases of property and equipment and software development in 2026 will total approximately $30 million to $40 million; primarily consisting of leasehold improvements and furniture and fixtures for certain office locations, information technology-related equipment to support our corporate infrastructure, and software development costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash spending is demonstrated, but its omission from the OE worksheet and the maintenance-versus-growth split remain unresolved. FY2025 capitalized software spending alone equals about 23% of the $88.9 million anchor, so a substantial maintenance omission is reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Trace each historical maintenance-capex deduction to the cash-flow statement, include capitalized software and cloud-implementation spending, support any growth classification with product-level evidence, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.134 million June 2026 fair-value liability, or about $2.01 per diluted share; $55.4 million maximum exposure, or about $3.26 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The unpaid acquisition consideration is a claim against common equity and should be deducted in the equity bridge independently of earnings remeasurement charges.
audit_findings.evidence: The remaining aggregate maximum amount of contingent consideration that may be paid in connection with the 2025 business combinations is $ 44.0 million, which is payable, if earned, on a staggered basis through December 31, 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted bridge claim is demonstrated. Deducting the recorded liability would reduce base value from $89.00 to approximately $86.99 per share, only 2.25% of base equity value; even deducting the filed maximum would reduce it to approximately $85.74. Neither changes the conclusion relative to the $155.27 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the latest $34.134 million fair-value liability, update it for subsequent payments or remeasurement, and show the $55.4 million maximum as sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Funded deferred-compensation assets may have been added without the matching liability
audit_findings.magnitude: $55.432 million June 2026 Plan assets included in stakes_net; approximately $3.26 per diluted share; latest matching liability amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Plan assets included in the stakes bridge are economically reserved for participants and require exclusion or an offsetting deferred-compensation liability.
audit_findings.evidence: This deferred compensation liability is fully funded by the Plan assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge inclusion is demonstrated because $33.816 million of convertible debt, approximately $0.1 million of equity investment and $55.432 million of Plan assets reconcile to the reported $89.3 million stakes_net. Removing the full Plan-asset amount would reduce base value to approximately $85.74 per share, 3.66% of base equity value, and would not change the conclusion relative to the market price. The exact net asset or liability requires the June Plan obligation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 deferred-compensation liability, remove both matched assets and liabilities from the bridge or include only any verified surplus available to common equity, and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Portfolio impairments may be counted both in owner earnings and asset values
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.396 million pretax FY2025 impairments; $26.262 million of FY2023 unrealized investment losses; effect on the $88.9 million trend anchor unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If investment losses remain in historical OE while the same investments enter the bridge at reduced values, the deterioration is charged once through OE and again through the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we recognized pre-tax $10.4 million of non-cash credit-related impairment charges related to our convertible debt investment in a third-party and non-cash impairment charges of $5.0 million on our equity investment in a hospital-at-home company.
audit_findings.explanation: The investment losses and reduced bridge values are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation retained or reversed those noncash losses. Because the anchor is a multi-year log trend rather than FY2025 OE, the resulting anchor and valuation effect cannot be established from the reported loss amounts alone.
audit_findings.action: Audit every OE-year reconciliation for separately bridged investment gains, losses and interest; remove those items consistently, recompute the log-trend anchor, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Performance-fee estimate true-ups may inflate normalized earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.0 million FY2025 variable-consideration true-ups; $22.8 million in FY2024, $9.6 million in FY2023 and $14.7 million in H1 2026; sustainable OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Persistent favorable prior-period revenue revisions can inflate normalized OE or growth if they are not collected, later reverse, or reflect systematic estimation bias.
audit_findings.evidence: Of the $1.70 billion total revenues recognized in 2025, we recognized revenues of $ 33.1 million from obligations satisfied, or partially satisfied, in prior periods, of which $ 31.0 million was primarily due to changes in the estimates of our variable consideration under performance-based billing arrangements and $ 2.1 million was primarily due to the release of allowances on receivables from clients and unbilled services.
audit_findings.explanation: The favorable true-ups are demonstrated and recur, but revenue amounts do not equal OE impact. The record does not show their margins, subsequent collections, reversals or treatment through working-capital adjustments, so materiality to the trend anchor remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Build an engagement-level history of true-ups, reversals and cash collections; reconcile it to contract assets and OE working-capital adjustments; normalize only any demonstrated persistent positive bias and rerun the trend anchor.
